rv.q: There's a wonderfully wistful sense to Michael Fentiman's quietly confident production; it takes gumption for a musical to be this dialled-down.
It sags slightly when there are too many soppy love songs...But the world feels merde, and this charming show brings some much-needed silly delight.
This production doesn't fix 'Amélie the Musical', but mon dieu it makes it fun.
This slice of Paris life comes alive.
This delightful, life affirming show is the perfect tonic to our gloomy, post-election, winter.

cn.t: Critics find this charming musical adaptation captures the whimsy of the beloved film better in London than on Broadway, though some question whether its sweetness can win over today's more cynical audiences.
